findings.statement: Section 9.2 stores final responses at idem:resp:{idempotency_key} and returns them on a hit "without touching DynamoDB". The key has no merchant scope and no request-hash comparison. Section 9.1 accepts merchant order or invoice numbers as keys, so two merchants can easily use the same key. When that happens, merchant B gets merchant A's payment object: cross-merchant data disclosure, and B's payment is never created even though B is told it succeeded. A reused key with a different body also gets the stored response instead of the HTTP 422 that FR-5 requires. This breaks P3 and FR-5.
findings.title: Redis idempotency fast path is keyed without merchant and skips the body-hash check
